messages.subject: csvToUMF: Mac vs Ubuntu
parts:
Hi all - I am hoping that someone with more knowledge of operating systems (Linux specifically) can help out. I have a script that works on my Mac. I am now trying to run it on a virtual machine that runs Ubuntu and I am running into trouble. This is my first time on an Ubuntu/Linux machine so I have no idea what could be wrong.

First off, as an FYI, I had to install R and all my packages on the virtual machine so these are all obviously the latest versions. This might not necessarily be the case for my Mac. I am listing the specs here in case this could be the difference.
Mac: R 3.4.3 (Kite-eating Tree), unmarked 0.12-2. I use RStudio to run scripts.
Virtual machine: R 3.4.4 (Someone To Lean On), unmarked 0.12-2. I run R from the command line here.

The problem is with using csvToUMF. On my Mac my site variables are correctly read in as site variables. However, on the virtual machine they are read in as observation-level variables. Nothing has changed for the rest with the script, file structure, input files...

One thing is that my script first puts all the required data together and saves it as a .csv file. Later in the script this is read in with csvToUMF. Is it possible that the way .csv files are created or written on Ubuntu are different than on a Mac? I looked at the generated .csv file and it looks fine.
